title: Muse Spark: fast or thoughtful
description: Thinking models and Muse Spark's modes: why a model thinks longer, when it's worth it, and how it works here.

steps.text: Some models reason before they answer: they write themselves a draft of their thoughts and work through the task step by step. These are called thinking models, and Muse Spark is one of them. Let's see why a model would think longer, and when it's worth it.

steps.definition: Before the final answer, it writes a hidden chain of reasoning and works through the task in steps. That makes it more accurate on hard problems, but it takes more time and more tokens.
steps.example: “Find the mistake in this calculation” — a thinking model goes through it step by step and catches it. For “what is 2+2” there's nothing to think about.

steps.imagePrompt: Three runners on a park track: one sprinting fast, one walking while reading a map, and a small team of three walkers comparing notes before choosing a path.
steps.caption: Fast, thoughtful or as a team — each mode has its own price

steps.definition: This is what the Meta AI app calls them. Instant answers right away, with no long reasoning. Thinking reasons step by step first. Contemplating runs several lines of reasoning in parallel and combines what they find.
steps.example: “What's the capital of France?” — Instant is enough. “Plan a workout for me with a bad knee” — that needs Thinking.

steps.text: Reasoning is made of tokens too. The model writes itself a draft of its thoughts. You usually don't see it, but you pay for it and wait while it's written. That's why Thinking is slower and costs more than Instant, and Contemplating costs even more, because there are several lines of reasoning.

steps.caption: The modes work as in the Meta AI app. Pick a question and a mode, then compare time, tokens and the answer. The numbers are an example

steps.question: If Thinking answers better, why not turn it on all the time?
steps.answer: On simple questions it answers the same as Instant — just slower and at a higher cost. Thinking pays off where the model would get it wrong without reasoning: multi-step tasks, calculations, plans.

steps.situation: An agent is setting a reminder: “call Mom tomorrow at 9.”
options: Instant — the task is simple and clear
Contemplating — let three of them think it over
Thinking — it can't manage without reasoning
steps.explain: This is one action with clear details. Long reasoning adds waiting time and tokens, and the result won't be any better.

steps.text: And here? This app calls Muse Spark through the API, not through Meta AI, and there is no mode switch: through the API, Muse Spark always reasons, even on “hi.” That's why the first answer doesn't arrive instantly — the model thinks first. What does speed things up is a short request and a chat that hasn't grown bloated.

This matters even more for an agent. An agent's turn is everything it does between your message and its reply, and in one turn it calls the model many times: think, call a tool, read the result. If every call is slow, a simple request can stretch to a minute. So where you can choose a mode, quick steps go to the fast mode, and reasoning is kept for plans and hard decisions.

In short. A thinking model reasons first, then answers: more accurate on hard tasks, but slower and costlier — reasoning is tokens too. In the Meta AI app, Muse Spark has three modes: Instant answers right away, Thinking reasons, Contemplating reasons along several lines at once. Through the API, as here, Muse Spark always reasons. Simple things fast, hard things thoughtfully.

questions.q: How is Thinking different from Instant?
options: It's a newer version of the model
questions.explain: Thinking writes a draft of its reasoning and only then gives the answer.

options: You pay for seconds of server time
questions.explain: The draft of thoughts is made of tokens, and tokens are what you pay for.

options: Thinks the same way, but writes longer
Reasons along several lines at once
questions.explain: Contemplating runs several lines of reasoning in parallel and combines what they find.

questions.q: How does Muse Spark work in this app?
options: Through the API — and it always reasons
In Instant mode, to be faster
It picks a mode to fit the question
questions.explain: Through the API, Muse Spark reasons on every request, and you can't turn that off. Instant, Thinking and Contemplating are a switch in the Meta AI app.
